## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the bar slot no longer collapses when the weather label is empty. At base, `visible` required a non-empty `label`, and `Bar.qml`'s module slot gives an invisible widget zero width. At head, the widget stays visible whenever the panel has loaded and shows the icon or a `—` placeholder. With coordinates saved, Open-Meteo is still requested without waiting for wttr.in, so a wttr.in TLS failure no longer hides the slot while that request is pending or failing. TLS verification is unchanged (no `-k`). The new `import "Model.js" as Model` in `BarWidget.qml` is valid; other plugins already import one `Model.js` from two QML files.

| Bar state | Base | Head |
|---|---|---|
| Panel loaded, `label` empty (fetch pending or failed) | hidden, zero-width slot | visible, `—` |
| Panel loaded, `label` set | visible, icon | visible, icon |
| Panel not loaded | hidden | hidden |

Two points in the description go beyond what the change does.

### Default location mode still gets no weather while wttr.in fails

Without saved coordinates (auto-detect, the default, or a name-only location), `refreshDailyForecast` gets Open-Meteo coordinates only from wttr.in's `nearest_area`:

```text
refresh()
 ├─ wttr.in request ── curl exit 60 ──> no report, no nearest_area
 └─ refreshDailyForecast()
      ├─ saved coordinates?  yes ──> Open-Meteo request ──> label set
      └─ no ──> needs wttr nearest_area ──> missing ──> return (no request)
```

At head this path shows a permanent `—` in the bar, and the panel stays on "Fetching forecast…". This is the second report in #11999 (panel stuck on "Fetching Forecast", icon back once coordinates are set by hand).

**Impact:** "Fixes #11999" would close the issue while the default configuration still shows no weather during a wttr.in outage. The description's "Open-Meteo path still sets label" applies only when coordinates are saved.

**Suggested change:** use "Refs #11999" or state that the fix covers the visible slot and the saved-coordinates case, leaving a non-wttr location source for a follow-up.

### "Keeps last good icon" does not hold across a remount or restart

`BarWidget.qml` calls `Model.resolvedBarLabel(panelLoader.item.label)` with one argument, so the `fallback` parameter is never passed in production. `Panel.label` starts as `""` on every new panel instance and is not saved anywhere. After a shell restart or a bar reload during an outage, head shows `—`, not the previous icon. Within one running panel, the last icon was already kept at base, because failed fetches never clear `label`.

**Impact:** the description's remount scenario and the test message "weather bar prefers a last-good fallback over the placeholder" describe behavior that production does not have.

**Suggested change:** either persist the last icon and pass it as `fallback`, or drop the unused parameter and its test and describe the result as "placeholder on remount, last icon while the panel stays loaded".

**Optional test improvement:** the three source-text assertions check that names appear in the file, not that they are wired in. Two synthetic edits to `BarWidget.qml` passed all 12 new assertions: adding `&& panelLoader.item.label !== ""` back after the `barWidgetVisible(...)` call, and setting the button text to `panelLoader.item.label` with `resolvedBarLabel` left only in a comment. The three `barWidgetVisible` assertions also cannot fail on a label change, because the function ignores its second argument. Anchoring the regexes to the full `visible:` and `text:` bindings would catch these regressions; `visible: !!panelLoader.item` would also remove the need for the helper.

**Optional:** the weather widget is in the default center layout, so an offline machine now shows a permanent `—` next to the clock, where other bar widgets hide when their resource is missing. If the placeholder stays, `WidgetButton`'s existing `dimmed` property could mark it as unavailable.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `1d0b597` against merge-base `86a2e58`; the weather files are unchanged on the current `quattro` tip. `test/shell.d/weather-test.sh` ran in an isolated sandbox through a Deno-backed `node` stand-in with its own controls: exit 0 with 69 passing assertions on head, and each of the 12 new assertions fails on base. Model functions and bar bindings were evaluated with synthetic Open-Meteo payloads. No live wttr.in or Open-Meteo requests, and no QML or desktop run, so the manual remount/TLS-failure check in the PR remains unverified. From source, it is not settled why the original reporter, with coordinates saved, saw the widget stay hidden rather than return once Open-Meteo answered.
